newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica Chamber of Mines urges Sunday working.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica Chamber of Mines urges Sunday working.

text.p: Trade unions must move in favour of working on Sundays and public holidays if mining is to make a significant contribution to reconstruction and development in South Africa, the Chamber of Mines said.

Speaking at the Chamber's 106th annual general meeting, outgoing president At du Plessis said on Tuesday that the Chamber would have to convince government to allow work-related issues to be negotiated by management and labour.

South Africa's minister of mineral and energy affairs Pennuell Maduna, also speaking at the AGM, told Chamber representatives that the government would work with the mining industry to enhance efficiency and productivity.

"Government and the mining industry can do a deal together. We in government will do our utmost to support you and see to it that South Africa's mines operate in a context where they can attract investment, encourage new development, minimise costs, maximise earnings and compete effectively internationally.
"You (the industry) in return should do your utmost to build up a mining industry where the ranks of all but the humble miner are no longer the exclusive domain of the few," Maduna said.
The mining industry has long attributed the decline in the industry's productivity to the increase in the number of statutory public holidays per year to 12 from seven.
The current government prohibition on Sunday work has further contributed to the decline, the industry says.

"Clearly, if mining is to make its best possible contribution to reconstruction and development...the Chamber will need to persuade government to adopt a more flexible approach and to place the determination of operational schedules in the negotiating arena shared by management and organised labour," du Plessis said.

Focusing on the Congress of South African Trade Unions, he added, "Cosatu seriously will have to reconsider the stance it has adopted in Nedlac (National Economic, Development and Labour Council) relating to Sunday work, public holidays and hours of work. A revision of attitude is essential to demonstrate Cosatu's sincerity in assisting the country to grow economically."
Du Plessis said developments in multi-skilling and flattening of managerial and supervisory hierarchies must continue as they promised productivity improvements.

"Commitment to the personal growth of employees will need to coincide with the creation of opportunities for promotion so that positions of seniority more equitably correspond with South Africa's population profile," he said.
But he added that due to the hazardous nature of mining, only suitably qualified individuals should occupy positions that entailed responsibility for colleague's lives.
